recipes.name: Grandma’s Corn Pudding
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup butter, melted and slightly cooled
1 (15.25 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a shallow 2-quart casserole dish.
Whisk eggs lightly in a large bowl.
Whisk milk and cornstarch together in a separate bowl until smooth and free of lumps. Add to the eggs with melted butter and sugar; whisk until well combined.
Stir in drained whole-kernel corn and cream-style corn until evenly combined.
Pour mixture into the prepared casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden brown and the center is set but still slightly jiggly, about 1 hour. Let rest briefly before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma’s Corn Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This creamy corn pudding, made with whole-kernel and cream-style corn, bakes in an hour for a sweet, custardy casserole perfect for holidays.

video.description: Is there anything more comforting than a delicious casserole courtesy of your grandma? In this video, we show you an easy-to-make recipe for grandma’s corn pudding with whole kernel corn and cream-style corn. Combined with a creamy egg mixture, the casserole is baked in the oven until golden brown.
video.name: How to Make Grandma’s Corn Pudding

review.reviewBody: I like to try and make things low-fat and healthy so I take recipes I like and alter them. This was a perfect example. I used 1 egg and 4 eggs worth of egg substitute. Butter is still healthier than margarine so I stuck with that. I also sprayed the dish with no-fat cooking spray. This dish STILL comes out fantastic and much more lowfat and heart-healthy.

Update: 11 years later and this is STILL a favorite Thanksgiving dish! I've started using 4 eggs and SOMETIMES adding some crushed buttery crackers. It always turns out great, it all gets eaten, and I love it so much!

The only thing I changed was that I only used 3 eggs and I thought it was AMAZING! When I ate it, I did add salt, but I'm a huge salt lover so that's totally a "to taste" thing. For those people who made comments about how this was "too much corn"... it's called CORN PUDDING... of course there's a lot of corn! If you don't like corn, this recipe isn't for you! If you like corn... enjoy, it's amazing!

I gave this three stars because the recipe should state that it needs to be made in a FLAT 2 quart casserole. The first time I made it, I used a flat casserole and it turned out perfect. My mom made it for christmas dinner this past week, but used a bowl type casserole and baked it for the full amount of time and it was very very runny. It looked like it was cooked through until we served it. Very disappointing the second time, but I will continue making it using my flat dish.

Definitely a keeper! My first time making it, I took some chances. I didn't want it sweet, so I omitted the sugar. I used about 2 cups of frozen corn with the 2 cans of cream corn. I added about 1/2 cup each of minced onion and red bell pepper to the butter when melting it, and sautéed until the onion was soft. After reading comments that it was too "eggy", I debated using 4 eggs instead of 5, but went ahead with 5 eggs. Oh, and I threw in about a tablespoon of chopped fresh oregano from the garden. It was great! It cooked much faster than expected in my oblong baking dish, and I had to keep it warm on a hot plate until serving time at the potluck, but it was delicious! And leftovers were great the next day too. Thanks for a very versatile recipe! I'll make it as written for Thanksgiving. Yum!

I have to make 2 batches of this every year for thanksgiving, my family is obsessed! I used to make it by the recipe but I’ve learned we like it better with 3 eggs instead of 5. I saw in the comments years ago to mix the milk and cornstarch together first and found that that is super helpful. I noticed some comments say this dish is bland, you can easily add whatever to make it more exciting but a little salt and pepper always do the trick.

This is a staple of the “big holidays” for our family. However, we have found that depending on the shape of the dish, it can take longer to cook. My alternative was to dole out 1 cup servings in ramekins and cook each serving as it’s own dish. I cut the sugar back by half to make it more savory and then put a brûlée top on it, and dubbed it Corn Brûlée. But I use this recipe as my staple every year.

I first liked this recipe, but I added my ex-mother-in-law's spin. Rest in peace, mommy #2. She made it with sweetened condensed milk, instead of regular milk. I discovered her secret. It is delicious as is, but for my southern family, sweeter is sweet, lol. Who knew this delicious treat would become a staple of our holiday meals? Thank you for the memories.

I was a little afraid to try this recipe but it's similar to a recipe my sister made last year and raved about. I read the comments and made some of the recommended changes. Also, I just don't like canned corn so I got fresh tri-color corn, blanched it, and cut it off the cob. This dish was DELICIOUS. Definitely on the sweet side, too, but not too much. I used 1-1/4 sticks of unsalted butter, 1/2 box of Krusteaz Honey Cornbread mix, and 1 egg. Beat that together then added the rest of the ingredients listed (used the tube of frozen white cream style corn). Put into a casserole dish and then it took almost 1.5 hrs. @ 350 degrees to cook (next to the Turkey/celebrated TG early). You can tell it's done when it's set in the middle and light golden brown. I forgot to take a picture, but everyone loved it. The texture was nothing like cornbread, but dryer than corn pudding. I added some dried Basil to half of the mixture and I loved it with and without the basil. I highly recommend this version.

This is my most favorite corn recipe--ever! When it's going to be the only recipe for lunch or dinner I add chopped brocolli or sliced asparagus or fresh green beans. If my old mind is functioning I also sprinkle alittle Cheddar cheese on the top before sticking in the oven. I usually have leftovers so I put the extra servings in small glass containers sprayed with Pam, snap on their lids and Vac Seal to retain freshness and flavor. Because they are smaller portions, I still bake at 400 but reduce the time to 25-30 mins. With fresh buttered rolls, this is a whole ' eats ' by itself. ENJOY!

Did not use sugar. did not use creamed corn. Did not use canned corn. Did not use starch. Just used frozen corn, straight out of the freezer. Heated milk. Put corn, milk, and butter in blender. Chopped setting, for a minute or 2. Added eggs, salt, pepper, and blended. Then I put chopped chives and set on blend for a short time. I poured into a shallow, buttered casserole dish. Baked in preheated oven at 400 for about an hour, until golden brown. Tastes like corn...not like sweetened canned corn!

I added a 4 oz can of drained chopped Green Chiles which added nice extra flavor. Mine came out a bit runny even though I drained the canned corn. BUT love this version with corn starch instead of flour which gave it a really nice true pudding texture. Maybe I will add another egg next time to combat the runniness.

I pretty much made it as written except I had some heavy cream I needed to use up and I did not have canned corn so I used frozen with the 2 cans of creamed corn... I used a little more corn starch after reading reviews... this is a super simple recipe with wonderful flavor. My son says "keep making it." I used an 11"x7" glass pan. Thank you for such a simple recipe

I’ve been making this for years and had to research the recipe again after not making it in a long time. I must say that I’m quite a fan of this creamy sweet side dish and for a thick version, I recommend adding more cornstarch. Thick savory buttery corn pudding you will get.

This tasted great but was a little "wet". I don't like the corn casserole with cornbread in it so thought I'd try this. I'll make this again and try to figure out how to make it a little dryer. Overall, it was very tasty!
It was good but needed something to give it a little more flavor. Have made very similar using Jiffy cornbread mix. Will try it again .
I like this recipe not use box of jiffy corn mix real corn pudding.Thanks Louisville kentucky

Tastes like cornbread, eats like Mac n cheese. Everybody at it, including the kids. I didn't use any creamed corn, just my home canned corn from our garden, 3 quarts, drained worked good for a double recipe. I added a good charge of freshly ground black pepper, and a few sliced leeks for the top. Plenty of leftovers for breakfast! Tasty!

Creamy and delicious. I had to tweak this quite a bit for lack of ingredients called for here but I only had whole kernel corn, no creamed, so I just took my hand emulsifier and pulsed the corn a few times, then added some half/half and sour cream to create a creamier texture which worked great. No cornstarch on hand, used flour. We love corn bread and now I’ll add this creamy version to our side dish rotation 👍
Loved it
Did omit the sugar and added half of a red onion, minced
